Who We Are
Barrow Hills is a lively and aspirational independent preparatory school and nursery for girls and boys aged 2-13.
We welcome children into a warm community set in an extraordinary woodland setting. Across our 33 acres, we harness forest school, eco-projects and adventurous education to promote sustainability, resilience and a deep connection with the natural environment.
Our specialist subject teachers bring a wealth of knowledge and use cutting edge technologies to deliver a curriculum that fosters critical thinking, creativity and future readiness. Curiosity and confidence drive high academic standards from Early Year Foundations Stage for our younger pupils to excellent Common Entrance results for our Upper Prep leavers.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Life | Private School Godalming | Barrow Hills
pageCache.text:
A place where every child can explore their creativity, express themselves with pride and discover their art
All our children take part in the performing and creative arts, which are a joyful and integral part of life at our school.
We nurture creativity and self-expression from an early age, with generous curriculum time and specialist teachers. Whether it’s a Shakespeare production, a musical, or pottery for our annual art exhibition, the arts are at the heart of school life.
We dance, sing, and create together. This engagement builds confidence, teamwork, and a strong sense of self. Our choirs, orchestras, ensembles, and collaborative art shows are all about encouragement, collaboration, and shared pride.
Many children go on to take art, drama or dance to scholarship level. But all benefit from a broad and deep education that extends far beyond the classroom — and it’s this richness that makes our children so happy and fulfilled.
Drama
Drama at Barrow Hills is for all, helping the building of confidence, creativity and expressive skills. Our pupils can perform, write, direct or contribute to technical theatre, supported by our highly skilled teachers. Opportunities are further enriched through workshops, visits from theatre companies, drama trips, and LAMDA sessions, in which over 40 pupils won awards last year. As part of the core English curriculum all pupils will prepare for a major production each year, with the recent repertoire for older pupils including ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’, ‘Lord of the Flies’ and ‘Annie’.
Music
Music at Barrow Hills is accessed by all our pupils, whether they are just beginning or developing advanced skills. Children benefit from 1:1 lessons, graded examinations, enrichment activities with visiting music teachers, and inspiring trips to live performances and events. We offer a very strong choral programme, including three choirs, with the eldest pupils able to perform at Bridewell Royal Hospital events. We are also fortunate to share a professional music department with King Edward’s Witley, and so offer a particularly high standard of specialist staff provision. We have a well provisioned music department, including a Mac suite for composition. We sing together, as a School, on a weekly basis and share that joy with our parents.
Dance
Dance encourages creativity, confidence and physical expression. Through structured classes, workshops and performances, children explore a variety of styles and have opportunities to perform in school shows and other special occasions, supported by expert teaching and visiting specialists.
Art & Design
Art and Design at Barrow Hills is vibrant, ambitious, and exceptionally well resourced. Our studios, set within the historic stable block, provide an inspiring creative environment, equipped with everything from a pottery kiln to 3D printers. Specialist teaching begins in Reception, led by our Head of Art and Design alongside visiting artists in residence.
Pupils experience both breadth and depth, exploring line, paint, sculpture, wood carving, print, textiles, fashion design, and 3D work, all underpinned by high expectations and excellent standards. Children contribute to our much-loved Annual Art Exhibition, when the Chapel is transformed into a gallery reminiscent of Tate Britain.
For pupils with particular talent or interest, our Art Scholarship Programme offers extension through portfolio development, art theory, and visiting artist workshops, including screen printing.
Our woodland setting strongly informs creative work, with sustainable, place-based projects such as the Living Willow Dome Classroom, designed and woven by the children. Art and Design is purposeful and connected, frequently linking with subjects such as Science to deepen understanding of the natural world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery Learning Foundations| Private Nursery | Barrow Hills
pageCache.text:
100% of leavers in 2026 received offers at their school of choice
We encourage children to set their sights high. We work to ensure that pupils flourish academically, socially and emotionally, enjoying a broad range of academic and co-curricular learning, social and enrichment activities and, very importantly, having great fun.
Our pupils excel academically from the Early Years Foundation Stage through to 11+ and 13+ examinations and scholarships. Much of this success stems from their genuine love of learning. We believe that quiet self-confidence grows from a deep connection with an area of personal interest.
We introduce specialist teaching from the age of two, ensuring that passions are discovered and developed early. Our sports, foreign language, computing and arts teachers work with children from the Early Years onwards. In addition, we offer a comprehensive co-curricular programme from the earliest stages of a child’s journey, giving pupils the agency to explore and deepen their individual interests and talents.
We believe that fostering quiet confidence and self-motivation equips our pupils to “achieve greater things” as they develop their life skills with us.
How do we achieve this?
We underpin rigorous academic outcomes with excellent, supportive pastoral care. Every child is not only known at Barrow Hills, but truly seen and understood. From hobbies and friendships to cognitive development, our Form Tutors serve as a cornerstone of guidance, supported by senior pastoral staff in each section of the school. Our enthusiastic Year 7 and Year 8 pupils act as exemplary role models for younger children through our House system and in everyday school life.
Character and skills development complement academic progress. Our key principles – being connected, active, compassionate, scholarly and curious – are woven consistently throughout our curriculum planning, reward systems and form times. We believe that the development of human skills is as integral to a forward-looking curriculum as knowledge and concepts, and parents see this philosophy brought to life during our weekly celebration assemblies.
We encourage pupils to take responsibility for their own learning within a supportive environment. Interactive, well-planned lessons and homework tasks, introduced from Pre-Prep, alongside purposeful use of technology, provide a strong scaffold for success.
Within lessons, pupils are encouraged to explore topics in greater depth and develop higher-order thinking skills. Older pupils also participate in timetabled ‘thinking skills’ lessons. Across subjects – from maths and geography to Forest School – problem-solving and investigative study are central to our curriculum delivery. Our approach to assessment and marking provides regular opportunities for self-reflection and a deeper understanding of each pupil’s learning journey.
At Barrow Hills, our creative programme is central to our success and offers every child the opportunity to explore and express themselves. All pupils have the chance to exhibit work in our annual Art Exhibition, building confidence and celebrating creativity. Regular trips to galleries and cultural events further inspire pupils to broaden their artistic horizons and engage with the wider art world.
We use our remarkable environment to deepen learning, and our library is a good example of this. A vibrant hub for learning and imagination – our pupils, and staff, simply love to read. Guided by a dedicated librarian, children benefit from initiatives that link closely to the curriculum, including themed days, Book Week and visits from authors. The library provides opportunities for reading for pleasure, research and creative projects, bringing learning to life and inspiring a lifelong love of books and knowledge. All children enjoy guided library sessions on a weekly basis as well as taking books home to enjoy. We have a beautifully appointed and resourced library, and this, alongside our English and Drama curriculum, drives our English attainment to exceed national standards at 11+ and at 13+ deliver an average A* to B grade in exams.
Barrow Hills School feels like a family: one with a great big garden, space to run and play, and a lot of love.
It’s lovely to see the children getting lost in their own imaginations, being creative, constructive and self-motivated, and progressing to their senior schools having taken advantage of the natural environment we offer.”
We like to think of Barrow Hill’s children as being ‘free-range kids’ who just get out there. For as we say at Barrow Hills, there is no such thing as bad weather, just bad clothing choices.

pageCache.pageTitle: Prep Co-Curricular | Independent Prep School Surrey | Barrow Hills
pageCache.text:
“Parents say that teachers find fun ways to ‘stretch and extend’ pupils” – Good Schools Guide
At Barrow Hills, we offer a broad, rigorous curriculum designed to spark curiosity and inspire children to explore their passions from an early age. We provide a nurturing and stimulating environment in which pupils are encouraged to embrace challenge, develop resilience and grow in confidence.
Our stunning woodland grounds give children the freedom to play, climb, run and unleash their imagination, while our classrooms combine challenge with careful support so that every child is known and cared for.
From Nursery and Kindy, a child’s love of learning begins to unfold at Barrow Hills. In the Pre-Prep years, we focus on building strong foundations of knowledge and a love for learning. As pupils move into Prep, we nurture confidence and support both academic and personal growth. By the time they leave Barrow Hills after Upper Prep, our pupils are not only achieving excellent academic results – often securing scholarships to their senior schools of choice – but are also highly motivated, independent learners, ready for the next stage of their education.
Small class sizes allow for an exceptional level of personalised attention. Specialist teachers are introduced from Nursery, ensuring that children’s interests are discovered and developed early. A strong emphasis on literacy and numeracy in the younger years is complemented by specialist teaching in sport, languages, computing and the arts, delivering a broad and inspiring education that sparks curiosity and creativity.
Pre-Prep Foundations (Reception, Years 1 & 2)
In Pre-Prep, children benefit from excellent facilities and specialist teaching in French, Forest School and PE. While we prioritise early literacy and numeracy through play-based learning, we also place great importance on personal, social and emotional development.
Pre-Prep staff closely monitor each child’s progress and set personalised targets for future development. We follow the Read Write Inc. phonics programme and are proud that our early learning outcomes consistently exceed both national and local averages.
In Years 1 and 2, pupils develop strong numeracy skills, including calculation and data presentation. There is a strong emphasis on reading and oracy, which underpin writing. Children come to appreciate writing as a powerful tool for communication – whether for entertainment, expression, description or explanation – ensuring they are well prepared for the next stage of their education.
Through child-led learning, we ensure every child feels valued and supported while building independence and self-esteem. Strong, open relationships with pupils and families are central to our approach, with the senior pastoral team meeting weekly to discuss each child’s development and provide tailored support. This close partnership enables us to make a meaningful difference, promoting empathy, kindness and a strong sense of belonging.
Prep Development (Years 3–6)
Our rigorous and inspiring Prep curriculum encourages pupils to embrace challenge, develop resilience and grow in confidence.
With specialist teaching in languages, science, music, art, design technology and sport, pupils develop expertise and confidence early on. Lessons are engaging and challenging, with personalised support to ensure each child thrives. We also guide pupils preparing to transition at Year 7 through the senior school application process, helping them approach exams and interviews with confidence.
Pupils learn to manage challenges, build strong friendships and grow into compassionate individuals who make a positive contribution to society. Older pupils are encouraged to mentor younger children, reinforcing our strong sense of community and ensuring every child has a role model. Outdoor education and enrichment activities – including clubs, trips and residential experiences – promote teamwork, independence and adventure.
Upper Prep Accomplishments (Years 7–8)
Upper Prep offers pupils the opportunity to enjoy life at the top of the school during a truly special stage of their development. Children mature within a safe, supportive environment alongside staff who know and understand them well.
Our focus extends beyond academic achievement to include the development of social confidence and emotional resilience, preparing pupils for life beyond Barrow Hills. We place strong emphasis on higher-order thinking and analytical skills, encouraging pupils to become independent learners and confident problem-solvers.
Leadership and responsibility are developed through a range of “captaincy” roles. Pupils apply and interview for positions aligned with their interests, from Head of House to Head of Art or Head of Gardening. Weekly leadership meetings provide opportunities to set personal goals and reflect on progress, supported by staff and peers. These experiences help prepare our Upper Prep pupils to be confident, considerate and ready for the next stage of their education.
We work closely with families to ensure each child progresses to the senior school best suited to their talents, ambitions and character. Our pupils move on with confidence to a wide range of leading independent schools.

pageCache.pageTitle: Future & Destinations | Surrey Prep Schools | Barrow Hills
pageCache.text:
Over 50% of children achieved A/A* at Common Entrance in 2025, with 40+ scholarships in all fields in the last 3 years
Our Head and Senior Team work closely with pupils to prepare them for entrance examinations and senior school interviews, ensuring a steady, confident and calm approach. This preparation combines a strong core curriculum with dedicated thinking skills, verbal and non-verbal reasoning, and mock examinations, all supported by detailed, individual feedback for both pupils and their parents on progress and key areas for improvement.
Our results speak for themselves – over the past three years, 98% have successfully gained a place at their first school of choice, with over 40 awarded scholarships.
Destination Schools
We are delighted to support our pupils in their transition to a broad range of high-achieving and well-considered senior schools after their time with us at Barrow Hills.
We work closely with families to ensure that each child progresses to the senior school that best suits their talents, ambitions and character. Our pupils move on with confidence to a wide range of leading independent and boarding schools.
Over the past three years, our most popular destinations have included King Edward’s School Witley, Churcher’s College, St Catherine’s School Bramley, Portsmouth Grammar School, Seaford College, Charterhouse, Cranleigh, and the Royal Grammar School.
For families aspiring to King Edward’s Witley, our Assured Places Programme ensures a seamless pathway all the way through to A-levels.
Academic Results & Destinations 2024/25
Scholarships
50% of our leavers gained senior school scholarships and awards in 2024
For many of our pupils, the additional challenge of pursuing a scholarship at 11+ or 13+ provides an opportunity to extend their studies and further develop their passions.
We pride ourselves on knowing our pupils very well, identifying their potential, and encouraging them to excel further. Additional support offered to those aspiring for Scholarships include:
Sports Scholars – extra tuition and training with our coaches, receiving nutritional advice, and developing leadership skills by mentoring younger children during lessons and tournaments.
Drama Scholars – participating in after-school clubs, attending workshops with professional directors and theatre companies, and enjoying additional theatre visits, together with support in preparing for auditions with casting agencies for film and theatre.
Art Scholars – learning to build a portfolio of work, conducting research on various artists, and experimenting with a wide range of media.
Over the last three years, our students have achieved 46 scholarships and awards from prestigious independent senior schools, including King Edward’s Witley, Charterhouse, Churcher’s College, Royal Grammar School Guildford, Seaford College, Ampleforth, and Prior’s Field. 40% were Sport Scholarships and 33% were Academic Scholarships.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wrap Around Care | Prep School Surrey | Barrow Hills
pageCache.text:
Supporting the needs of our thriving Barrow Hills community with engaging before and after-school care
The Barrow Hills community is busy and thriving. We offer wrap-around care until 6.00pm, where children can enjoy a light meal, do their homework, play with friends, and make the most of our beautiful grounds.
Whether arriving directly by School minibus or by car, our children can book in for Breakfast Club for a soft start and nourishing breakfast at 7.45am.
For children in the Prep we always have staff on duty, in the playground, from 8am every morning allowing parents to ‘stop and drop’ for an early getaway.
After School Care – Pre-Prep Department
Children in Pre-Prep (Nursery – Year 2), can join the wraparound care ‘Club’ at the end of the school day – where they either play games and activities in one of our warm classrooms, or if the weather allows, run around in the glorious Pre-Prep gardens. Club is available until 6.00pm once the children are in Kindy and have had their 3rd birthday. For our youngest children in Nursery, Club is available until 4.30pm.
After School Care Prep Department
For children in the Prep and Upper Prep (Years 3 – 8) supported after school study ‘Club’ lets children complete their homework before they head home to relax and unwind after their busy day. A hot meal is provided at 4.45pm and children are able to stay safely and happily until 6.00pm.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Life | Private School Godalming | Barrow Hills
pageCache.text:
Quiet confidence and self-motivation above, beyond and outside the classroom
At Barrow Hills, learning goes beyond the classroom with a comprehensive programme of activities at School and exciting trips for pupils of all ages. Our pupils explore new ideas through workshops and real-world experiences, helping them grow both academically and socially and making learning more fun, meaningful, and unforgettable.
We host a wide range of workshops each year to enrich the curriculum at Barrow Hills. Recent examples include STEM workshops offering insight into applied physics, delivered in partnership with the McLaren race team, and biology workshops led by a leading conservationist. In the humanities, we have enjoyed hosting Viking re-enactments, as well as visits from well-known authors, actors and artists. We also work closely with the Fire Service and medical professionals, rolling up our sleeves to support practical, and in some cases life-saving, applications of learning.
Alongside this, we offer a broad programme of visits and trips that enables our pupils to explore the world around them. We balance short day trips, to farms, museums and galleries closely linked to our curriculum in art, history, geography, sciences and literature, with more adventurous overnight residential experiences. Opportunities for independence and immersion are carefully staged, beginning in Year 3 with a residential at the Sayers Croft Environmental Centre, and developing further as pupils grow older through adventurous sport in Snowdonia or language immersion in France.
We also take our sports teams and choir ‘on tour’, and during school holidays we offer exciting additional opportunities, such as a ski trip.

pageCache.pageTitle: New Year Honour for Mr John Towers, Member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE) - Barrow Hills
pageCache.text:
Stay connected with the latest news, achievements and events from across Barrow Hills
New Year Honour for Mr John Towers, Member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE), Head, Barrow Hills School, Witley, Surrey
It is with immense pride and pleasure that we announce that our esteemed Bridewell Royal Hospital colleague, Mr John Towers, Head, Barrow Hills School, has been appointed a Member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE) for services to education in the King’s 2026 New Year Honours.
Education was a driving force in John’s young life, sparking a passion for accessible and transformative learning for all. Throughout his 30 year career, John has dedicated himself to the service of others, nurturing pupils and young educators through leadership and coaching and through his extensive charitable endeavours. As Director of Education for the ‘Reach to Teach’ charity, John spent four years building over 100 village schools in remote parts of rural India. He has served several terms as a trustee at the Royal Society of the Arts.
Since joining Barrow Hills, a School of the Bridewell Royal Hospital foundation, as Head in 2023, John has been instrumental in shaping the future direction and successes of the School and more widely within the foundation, creating the broadest opportunities for pupils at every educational stage. An advocate for inclusion and educational excellence, John drives academic, pastoral and co-curricular quality at Barrow Hills, and ensures technological distinction through our unique Bridewell AI system, future-proofing pupils’ education for a changing world, responsibly and ethically.
John’s dedication, vision, and selfless service truly embody the values we cherish within the Bridewell Royal Hospital foundation.
On his award, John reflected “I’m deeply grateful to receive an MBE, and share my sincere appreciation of working with so many dedicated colleagues across the state, independent, and international education development sectors. It’s great to celebrate this award with our wonderful team at Barrow Hills. Within Bridewell Royal Hospital, our charitable foundation of nearly 475 years, we are dedicated to the delivery of excellent outcomes with kindness and compassion. As in all the educational settings in which I’ve served, I want all our pupils to be inspired to do well and to do good.”
Please join us in congratulating John on this truly well deserved honour and remarkable achievement.
The official announcement appears in the London Gazette and national newspapers.

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery Forest School & Ecology | Goldaming | Barrow Hills
pageCache.text:
Our woodland setting immerses our children in hands-on learning that sparks wonder, builds confidence, and nurtures skills for life
At Barrow Hills, our 33 acres of woodland, including three dedicated Forest School areas, provide a unique and enriching environment for learning from Nursery through to Year 8. Children in Pre-Prep enjoy at least one weekly Forest School session, led by our qualified team, embracing all weathers with warm clothing and wellies.
Our woodland is teeming with wildlife, from jays and squirrels to deer and foxes, creating a stimulating, multi-sensory environment that sparks imagination, discovery and a lifelong connection with nature. Outdoor play and learning also enhances the development of verbal and non-verbal communication skills; it’s a key reason for our assessment scores at the end of the Early Years Foundation Stage consistently well exceeding national expectations.
We nurture a supportive learning environment where pupils are encouraged to take measured risks and try new things, allowing growth through these experiences. By stepping slightly outside their comfort zones, pupils develop confidence and resilience as they learn to manage uncertainty in a supportive environment.
Ecology: Nurturing a Sustainable Future
To strengthen our connection with the natural world, we have invested in a wide range of ecological initiatives, shaped by pupil feedback, and embraced our natural environment as a rich source of inspiration and education. In 2024, Barrow Hills was shortlisted in the Independent School of the Year awards for Environmental Achievement.
We have up-skilled cohorts of ‘Ecology Captains’ in sustainability, biodiversity, and local and global ecology. This enthusiastic and growing group of children thrives on having agency and stewardship over our environmental initiatives. Peer-to-peer learning is now substantial, with younger pupils looking up to their older peers. Eco Warriors and Gardening Club are seen as exciting and valuable roles within the school.
A standout project has been the creation of our willow dome, an outdoor learning space for Prep children. This initiative complemented our Eco Schools Accreditation for 2024, where Barrow Hills was awarded another Green Flag, with Distinction, the highest possible level. Additionally, we received a ‘Highly Commended’ award from the Primary Schools Green Awards.
For us, nature is more than a setting – it is a teacher, a playground, and a source of inspiration. Every child benefits from hands-on learning, enabling their academic, social and emotional growth, and giving them the chance to make a real difference in caring for our world.
“If you lie on the floor and look up into the trees, you can see things you’ve never seen before!”
“Finding bugs and worms is my favourite thing… did you know that worms breathe through their skin?”

pageCache.pageTitle: Why Our Prep School Nursery? | Private Nursery | Barrow Hills
pageCache.text:
A warm environment that benefits from the breadth of our outstanding Prep School
Children can join our Nursery from their 2nd birthday. We provide a warm and nurturing environment in which your child can play, learn and develop with all the benefits of our outstanding Prep School.
Why our Prep School Nursery?
Your child will establish a relationship with the school within their first term with us and maintain this throughout their time here. Their early friendship group and familiarity with the setting are key reassurances for a family when choosing the right setting.
Learning
Our Nursery follows the Early Years Framework Curriculum and the seven areas of learning, with a balance of learning through play, as well as more focused adult-led learning. The staff have created an exciting curriculum which prepares the children for school, at a pace they feel most comfortable with.
Specialist Teachers
Our highly experienced specialist teachers significantly enhance the curriculum every week in subjects including Music, French, Sports and Forest School. Beyond Nursery, the amount of specialist teaching increases and the children also begin visiting the Science Labs for the first time from Reception. They are taught Art by our Head of Art in the art studio as well as IT and Drama.
Phonics
Our ‘Kindy’ class are introduced to phonics through the Read Write Inc programme which supports their literacy progress, including developing their language through story times and teaching phonics.
Meal Times
The Nursery children eat their hot lunch in the school dining room, alongside the rest of Pre-Prep. As well as promoting a healthy and balanced diet, good manners are encouraged as children eat their lunch at the table together with the nursery staff.
Performances
Our Nursery is an important part of our school community, and both Nursery classes are involved in Pre-Prep performances each term.
Parent Consultations
In addition to daily updates on Tapestry, our Kindy class have Parent Consultations which take place during the autumn and spring terms. There is also an end of year school report at the end of the summer term.
Our small and friendly department enables our highly experienced staff time to really build strong relationships with each child and their family.

pageCache.pageTitle: Leadership Opportunities | Prep, Goldaming | Barrow Hills
pageCache.text:
“Barrow Hills has the environment, learning culture and pastoral care balanced perfectly to nurture success” – Good Schools Guide
At Barrow Hills, care sits at the heart of school life. Strong connections are built through our Tutor and House systems which nurture friendship, foster a sense of belonging and shape community through shared events and collective celebrations. Through this connected approach, children develop confidence, empathy and a strong sense of responsibility for one another.
We welcome parents to our weekly Friday celebration assemblies which exemplify the breadth and depth of pupil care, achievement and talent – from sporting success and technological innovation to acts of kindness. Our curriculum is intentionally broad, and we invest in both time, pastoral care and specialist teaching. This hat–trick of investment has a tangible, positive impact on well-being and strong achievement flows from this.
Our Tutorial System
At the heart of our wellbeing approach is a dedicated Form Tutor to know every child. Working with small form groups, tutors are able to offer meaningful one-to-one support and build a deep understanding of each individual learner. This enables us to tailor teaching, support and interventions effectively for each pupil.
Across each section of the school, Heads of Year lead and coordinate pastoral care, ensuring continuity and smooth transition from Pre-Prep through to Senior School and beyond. Our strong personal knowledge of pupils is supported by year-on-year validated tracking of attitudes to self and school. Our pupils, compared with national data, demonstrate an outstanding sense of wellbeing, confidence in their capabilities, readiness for learning, self-worth and a strong work ethic. We also place high value on pupil voice, through regular School Council representation and active participation in departmental reviews.
Our House System
Our pupils love being part of our House system, representing one of three Houses: Kean, McCormack and Murtough. Each House creates a strong sense of belonging and provides a family within a family at Barrow Hills, offering opportunities for vertical mentoring, with older pupils, including trained ‘Captains’, acting as positive role models for younger children.
House achievements are celebrated weekly in assembly, and regular House meetings bring pupils and staff together; all teachers are also members of a House. Competitions run throughout the year and include singing, poetry, creative writing and sport. The Houses also lead our outward-facing charitable work, supporting initiatives such as local care homes and a partner special school.
Our pupils are really passionate about collecting House Points, for the team and for themselves. Teachers link the award of House points to our Pupil Profile attributes: being curious, brave, scholarly, compassionate, generous, joyful, truthful and responsible.
Young Leadership and Mentoring
At Barrow Hills, pupils begin developing leadership skills early, for example through representation on the School Council. As they move through the school, every pupil has the opportunity to take on a leadership role, particularly in the formative Upper Prep years.
Our Upper Prep curriculum and experiences prepare pupils for life beyond Barrow Hills, developing not only academic strength but also essential soft skills such as collaboration and the foundations of entrepreneurship.
Pupils apply for a wide range of roles, including Head Boy or Head Girl, Head of House, and captaincies across areas such as sport, drama, art, literacy, science and Pre-Prep. Many also serve as Peer Mentors or Wellbeing Ambassadors, supporting younger pupils.
Strong vertical relationships are a hallmark of school life. Children of different ages often play together, reflected in our most recent external review, where 100% of pupils reported that they feel entirely safe – with space to breathe, belong and grow.
Enrichment opportunities
Enrichment groups in sport, art and drama, alongside academic enrichment interventions, help the children prepare for scholarships, as well as extending their interests and love of learning.
Developing resilience and independent learning skills is a key focus at Barrow Hills. Children are encouraged to read widely, listen to podcasts and talks, and practise effective revision strategies taught within lessons. All pupils have timetabled guided library sessions. Study skills workshops and drop-in support sessions help pupils consolidate learning and build confidence.
At Barrow Hills, we also recognise the importance of developing pupils’ practical skills in Years 7 and 8. Through our Upper Prep Enterprise Project, the children learn about working as a part of a team, how to develop their problem-solving skills and how to manage money. This now runs alongside future facing studies such as our TEDS curriculum (Technology, Engineering Design and Sustainability).
Across all these initiatives we lay the groundwork for children to travel onwards with skill and confidence, thinking deeply, listening well and achieving their very best.
Our teaching incorporates the best of academic and creative practice and is delivered using state of the art technology.
